purpose: 351 remaining consumer traces, authored against the specified input; historical and live/target-dependent conclusions kept distinct.

chains.consumerAndConfiguration: OpenAIProvider instance is consumed by ContextManager token counting, projection and split assertions; this instance has no chat dispatch in those tests. Separate local network instances are recorded independently.

Literal API key enters OpenAIProvider chat/chatStream through ContextManager or AgentRunner; baseURL is assembled from this test's createServer listen(0,127.0.0.1) address. No environment URL override is passed to that instance. Receiver returns synthetic model responses and closes in finally.

Dead owner token is written as memory lock metadata in a mkdtemp workspace. Consumer is StructuredMemoryStore lock recovery, using an exited child PID and current hostname; it is not a network authentication token.

Supervisor harness places pnpm/node/curl substitutes first in PATH before serve-e2e.sh; assigned admin password goes only to those substituted bootstrap/service invocations. Fake services exercise process lifecycle; no real DB initialization in this harness.

Runtime wrapper forwards DB_PASSWORD to actual approval/observation/canonical MySQL tests. Host/port/user can select an existing server; child tests create their own schemas but the wrapper does not own the SQL server. Missing DB_PASSWORD previously became an implicit empty password; now rejected before runtime child/log creation, explicit empty still forwarded. Caller must authorize the target and credential.

run-environment derives a per-run database/container/password, sets MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD at docker run, obtains the published loopback port from that same container and sends the same password to readiness/init/assertions/dump/restore. Restore schema derives from that run. Container trap is confined to its run name; derived password is a disposable fixture, not evidence about any shared account.

Recovery observation passes its fixture password to docker exec and the child recovery test. run-report-recovery creates the named disposable container with the same password and supplies its docker port; direct invocation accepts a name and port, so caller must preserve that pair. Docker inspect records identity but does not independently prove that an arbitrary supplied port belongs to the container.

serve-e2e generates qualification_jwt_secret using node crypto randomBytes; same in-memory value is passed to the started API HTTP/WS service. DB_NAME is the qualification schema; managed Playwright refuses server reuse. This is fresh signing material, not a committed signing value; caller's DB configuration still needs authorization.

run-existing-mysql takes an explicit password and configurable host/port/user/container, creates a per-run qualification schema and sends that password through init/assertions and subprocess server. Its docker CLI target and TCP target are supplied independently; schema prefix limits cleanup, not server identity. Requires caller/owner correspondence and window before real use.

The unselected manifest entry is deliberately unreadable. loadTestResource reads only the selected temporary resource; assertions verify no unselected secret read. File value is a fixture path marker, not an authentication input.
safeLogs receives a constructed string and assertions reject its sentinel and terminal controls. No driver/login consumer.

Archived audit reproduction injects authenticateAccessToken and a synthetic provider into DirectAdapter, opens a local WS instance and sends the probe token there. Relative imports are historical and not a current test entry. It does not establish live Gateway authentication or current correctness of that old reproduction.

Literal is passed to the test's environment/configuration parser and asserted as a returned config. Real acceptance blocks separately read explicit operator configuration; these particular parser inputs do not initialize a SQL client.

row() returns synthetic users to the test's pool/query implementation; MysqlInvestigationStore and ActorContextService consume those rows for list authority. password_hash is only a service/user discriminator, not login password verification.

Synthetic request snapshot is JSON inserted into the test-created governance schema through its injected pool, then consumed by usage/redaction tests. Connection password is a different injected AUTH_TEST_MYSQL_PASSWORD; matched value is not passed as driver authentication. Server ownership still depends on the caller's test port.

prepareEvidence/publicDocument/tool execution receives explicitly constructed canary fields; assertions verify redacted public/tool evidence. SQL-backed variants persist in their created schema and use separate environment DB credentials; synthetic LLMProvider implementations do not call a real model. Does not prove caller SQL endpoint ownership.

OpenAIProvider is wrapped/exercised for countPromptTokens/projectMessages/split before assertions. This occurrence does not dispatch a provider request; separate network instances use their own local receiver and are recorded separately.

SystemEventBridge handler receives an explicit unknown-component payload canary; workflow/jobs are queried to verify it was not persisted. DB uses a created schema on caller's loopback test port. This token is not supplied as SQL or HTTP authentication.

Registered synthetic read tool returns password canary to execution recovery/evidence handling with controlled LLMProvider. Canonical state is in the test-created schema using environment DB credentials; returned field is not used to connect to a target.
validateInvestigationProfile rejects an added apiKey property on an otherwise valid read-only profile. Value is a negative schema input, with no provider construction or HTTP dispatch.

NotificationService.send receives email/Feishu/OAuth fixture channels; sendEmail or postJsonToVerifiedTarget is spied and resolves before transport. Signing/validation may run, but the matched credentials cannot reach SMTP/Feishu through these test cases.

Resource enumeration services are mocked and return synthetic password/ciphertext fields; registered list route projects public DTOs through app.inject. Matched values are returned rows, not driver connection configuration.
SNMPv3 fixture is supplied to resource network-device type/schema validation across algorithm combinations. This test does not instantiate a transport/session or dispatch packets.

Credential update invokes MonitorCollector through mocked database service and unifiedCollector.collectInstance; configuration refresh is asserted at that mocked receiver. No target connection with the literal is opened.

NetworkDeviceCollector receives injected store() and adapter() whose probe/system/interfaces functions return synthetic observations. Credentials flow into that adapter, not the native SNMP transport.
HuaweiAdapter receives explicit client objects implementing get/table with fixture varbind arrays; SNMP credentials flow into that client. Native SNMP session factory is never selected here.
NetworkDeviceDatabaseService receives poolFor(execute) and db-connection is mocked. SNMP secrets reach encryption and captured mock SQL bindings, not a real SQL server/device.

Partial SNMP config is among invalid create/update payloads exercised against the owned test schema. Probe/SSH recipients are injected controlled receivers; actual SQL config is supplied separately and schema lifecycle is task-owned. The partial canary is not issued as real device credentials.

SnmpClient receives injected session factory/session() methods; credentials are supplied to that factory, whose get/bulk paths are fake. Assertions exercise authorization/errors/cancellation without native device I/O.

Fastify app.inject invokes network-device test-connection route with injected probe/sshProbe and mocked persistence. Unknown/missing fingerprint inputs reject before probe; valid inputs go to the spy, not a real SNMP/SSH client.
RbacService's injected dbConnection.execute rejects with constructed sensitive storage text; read endpoint/error assertions verify fixed public errors. Literal is only an Error message.

Legacy AuthDatabaseService tests use explicit in-memory CAS pool and separately an opt-in test-created MySQL schema. OLD/NEW inputs are hashed/compared as synthetic users seeded by this test. Actual DB authentication comes from separate AUTH_TEST_MYSQL configuration; account test is real in opt-in mode, server ownership remains caller responsibility.

WS tokens enter DirectAdapter started by the test; authenticateAccessToken is explicitly injected (resolved, deferred, or rejected) and chat persistence is mocked. The client connects to that adapter's local selected port. Tokens select test cases, not production JWT signatures.
bodyWithRole enters user request schema contract checks; rejected legacy role is compared to allowed contract. RbacService database is mocked; this particular value does not create a real user.

Synthetic signing key is passed to JWT sign/verify for a locally started Fastify notification-records fixture. Optional MySQL case uses separately injected credentials and created schema. Key does not configure a shared API; matched value is used for local bearer signatures.

Global fetch is replaced with a function asserting the Microsoft URL and forwarding to this test's HTTP server on listen(0,127.0.0.1). Synthetic refresh/access values reach only that OAuth receiver and local smtpRecipient; refresh persistence is a spy. No call to Microsoft is made through this path.

CustomSQLProvider gets a DatabaseConnection with query/execute functions supplied by record(). Its config password is descriptive metadata; provider executes queries on the injected object and never opens a driver from that password.

NotificationDatabaseService db-connection and encryptData are mocked; config/ciphertext values feed mocked execute/getConnection transaction bindings and assertions. No real SQL or notification delivery occurs at those occurrences.

Acceptance helper instance() supplies placeholder config fields but overwrites pool/pgClient/oracleConnection/dmConnection with an already opened driver. Actual driver authentication is profile.password from explicit engine-specific config. Literal placeholder is never passed to driver creation; real profile resource access remains opt-in and caller-owned.

exchangeMicrosoftSmtpRefreshToken receives synthetic refresh input; each case replaces global fetch and returns constructed Response or controlled cancellation. Access/rotated values are mock response/expected output, not Microsoft account tokens.

InstanceDiagnosticContextService uses dependencies()/guarded test functions returning synthetic resource/connection data. Matched password/ciphertext/dynamic-key fields feed bounded context projection and assertions; no driver is constructed from those values.
System audit route consumes app.inject payload via MemoryAuditLogStore; assertion checks password is excluded from recorded audit. No external credential use.

Audit boundary test posts constructed password canary to its local Fastify server; redacted record is mirrored/persisted through a created audit schema. AUDIT_BOUNDARY_MYSQL_CONFIG supplies actual SQL authentication separately; canary is only body data.

MonitorCollector gets rows from mocked database/instance services; unifiedCollector and dbConnection are mocked. Opaque ciphertext feeds capability/collection scheduling tests and does not decrypt into a real connection here.

runtime-provider test's fixture() starts local HTTP receiver returning an error containing the constructed credential text. SDK baseURL is that receiver. Consumer under test suppresses the upstream error; literal is response canary, not issued media credentials.

socketAdapter starts a test DirectAdapter with controlled provider/authority; a second auth frame deliberately uses invalid token and must close. Canonical run SQL uses separate environment credentials and task-created schema. Second token is never accepted as real account authentication.

DirectAdapter test creates local WS receiver and injects authenticateAccessToken/revalidateActor stubs plus Mock/Catalog/Failing providers. Matched token is sent to that local adapter and interpreted by the injected authority; no platform JWT/key reuse is proven by this synthetic token.

DirectAdapter receives explicit actorContextService returning fixture actor and controlled provider; probe/steer frames enter local adapter listener. Persistence services are mocked/spied for this path. Token is only fixture transport data.
SnmpDiscoveryCache.get hashes/keys a constructed config array; no SNMP client/session is invoked in this test.

readLegacyPublished/decodeBindingPayload receives malformed envelope/override canary. Expected BindingPersistenceError has fixed code and excludes payload; neither routine connects using the canary URL/password.
app.inject sends forbidden extra credential properties to MetricPolicy routes backed by MemoryPolicyStore and testResources; validation rejects payload before persistence/target access.
parseJournalJson receives stringified synthetic journal fields containing canary; output projection/redaction is asserted before truncation. No SSH call occurs in this test case.
freezeEvidence receives a constructed SQL/password object and freezes sanitized evidence; AnalysisDispatchStore pool throws if an unvalidated write is attempted. Matched value is redaction input.

Notification credential fixture signs JWT for its local Fastify app, persists synthetic channels in max590 random schema and uses controlled HTTP/SMTP recipients; node:https request is mocked and OAuth fetch is stubbed to constructed responses. Actual SQL login comes from NOTIFICATION_CREDENTIALS_MYSQL_JSON. Synthetic signing/refresh/channel fields are not shared credentials; caller SQL server authorization still required.

ssh2.Client is replaced with a class whose connect/exec/error events are controlled by the test. Secrets exercise pool invalidation, authorization window and close behavior; no native SSH connection uses them.

Readiness/config diagnostics receives an explicit environment object and returns only selected settings; JWT field is an exclusion canary, not assigned to process environment or server signer by this occurrence.

Delivery recovery test injects exchangeMicrosoftSmtpRefreshToken behavior returning synthetic access token after abort; HTTPS request is mocked and SMTP recipient is controlled. Workflow state uses separately configured SQL pools/schema. Access canary is not sent to Microsoft.

WorkerRuntime receives an object store implementing claim/heartbeat/complete/fail; constructed job payload reaches controlled handler and StructuredLogEvidenceAdapter. Assertions verify payload exclusion; no external authentication consumer.

Notification preparation mocks dbConnection, SMTP OAuth exchange, HTTPS and outbound policy; encrypted refresh marker is channel fixture consumed by those controlled dependencies, not real ciphertext for a remote account.
discoverModels points to this case's createServer/listen(0,127.0.0.1) origin, drains body and returns known model list. API key is sent only to that receiver; finally closes it.

publicProvider allowlist projection receives synthetic nested secret/ciphertext/extra fields; assertions exclude them and retain allowed model data. No provider client is constructed from those fields.
parseBackupArtifact receives a copied backup with forbidden ciphertext property; expected result is PROVIDER_CONFIG_BACKUP_SECRET_DETECTED. This tampered object is not passed to restore or persisted.

ProviderConnectionService gets injected store whose fake saved key and opaque marker are consumed by connection-test routes. Provider URL comes from local fixture server and fake saved key is returned by getProviderApiKey spy; no opaque marker is decrypted as production ciphertext.
discoverModels gets explicit fetcher vi.fn returning constructed model Response. draft key is an argument to this fake fetcher, never global network fetch.

Credential destination policy uses in-memory provider/store and outbound/service spies. Ciphertext sentinel selects saved-key reads/decryption failures; destination changes are checked before transport. No real stored provider is read or mutated.

These occurrences are string patterns used inside a console.error spy to detect leakage of the separately injected profile password. The pattern is not a literal connection password; no driver receives it.

dbConnection.initialize(bad) sends a deliberately invalid synthetic password to the explicit profile endpoint, verifies disconnected state, then uses profile.password for the valid test. Schema is task-created, server is caller-supplied; real negative authentication requires resource authorization.

SshSessionPool.execCommands gets fakeClient/FakeChannel; command text is a privacy canary consumed by local timeout/error path. It is not an authentication secret and no SSH server runs those commands.

TypeBox Value.Check/public API contract tests receive synthetic ciphertext and SNMP config objects. Matched fields are schema input, not live service/driver configuration; no network sender in this path.

get-instance-summary tool uses mocked instanceDatabaseService/RbacService; opaque ciphertext is returned row data then public output is asserted. No connection to a database instance uses that ciphertext.

request helper builds fetch URL from the Fastify test instance's actual listen(0,127.0.0.1) address and supplies a synthetic authorization header. Used to test platform observation/log exclusion, not platform login.

write-release-manifest-buffer test creates a temporary source tree containing a fabricated token assignment and executes release manifest scanner against it. It is a scanner negative fixture, not imported executable source or authentication input.

SourceManagementService is restricted to this fixture's local upstream origin and receives a one-use synthetic HTTP token through an in-memory store or test-created MySQL schema. Receiver validates the test header; redirect and audit assertions use local servers. MySQL credentials, if enabled, come from separate explicit test config.

Runtime event contains fabricated content/apiKey, platformLogs.record is spied into a local StructuredLogEvidenceAdapter; assertions reject unsupported content fields. No model/provider call receives the value.
public DTO/sensitive-data routines consume explicitly constructed nested credentials/ciphertext and assert allowlist/redacted output. This input is never passed to driver/authentication code.

DeviceAuthService test starts its own DirectAdapter with injected actor authentication, then sends deviceAuth plus synthetic bearer marker to that WS. Device registration uses explicit DEVICE_AUTH_TEST_MYSQL_URL and task-created schema; marker is not a platform JWT. Caller must authorize the SQL target.

AgentToolAuditService gets captured execute implementation; args/result/source code strings are privacy canaries serialized for audit and asserted redacted. execute_code text is never executed by this test.

CredentialReferenceService receives explicit fake executor/transaction connection and decrypt callback. Encrypted marker is a fake row returned by that executor, exercised for ownership/consumption/rollback; no real credential database or external operation uses it.
Knowledge service string sanitization receives a multi-assignment canary; output must remove secret text. It is not evaluated as JavaScript/shell or used as authentication.

Knowledge API submits a canary in actions text to its local server/store for sanitization and retrieval. Test fixture supplies created operations schema and KnowledgeService canary list; no action text is executed. DB endpoint remains caller-selected.
rejectSourceHttp consumes constructed Response.json with token/header canaries and rejects with bounded receipt; no outgoing fetch is made by this test.
validateNotificationChannelConfig consumes SMTP/OAuth and encrypted config samples and asserts accepted/rejected shape. No NotificationService.send or real SMTP/OAuth operation occurs.

smoke-test AUTO_BODIES -> getBody -> runOne fetch POST /api/users is an authenticated write to SMOKE_BASE_URL (default development API); no server/account bootstrap or cleanup ownership is enforced by this CLI. Removed fixed created-user password in favor of crypto-random per-process value. Existing target and write authorization remain caller prerequisites; this change does not authorize running it on shared services.

Instance create/update -> InstanceDatabaseService.authorizeDatabaseTarget -> encryptData -> pool.execute INSERT/UPDATE in task-created metadata schema. These service methods do not open a target connection; dbConnection.getPool is replaced with that schema pool and removal stopTasks is injected. Synthetic password is persisted metadata, not SQL login authentication. Actual metadata SQL server still uses separate caller-injected credentials.

PG test passes explicit synthetic admin/reader/wrong passwords to pg.Client on W03_PG_PORT, stores reader credential in w03_metadata, and exercises real collection. run-pg-collection supplies disposable MySQL/PG ports and account initialization. Direct invocation checks host/schema/port but cannot independently prove container ownership; preserve runner pairing and caller authorization.

createCredentialProbeFixture uses in-memory provider/store with fake encrypted marker; saved key is returned directly by the fake getter, SDK request goes to fixture createServer's random loopback origin. No database is opened or real ciphertext decrypted.

provider-config backup drill inserts known synthetic Provider key into its random max-drill schema, exercises backup/restore with this local key and verifies no leaked key. SQL auth is separate DB_* input; no model generation is requested. Caller endpoint ownership remains required.

database-recovery.real opts in, creates a disposable container and starts API with generated password and per-run ports; request helper sends invalid refresh token to that API and expects 401. No real refresh token is being reused.

Lost encryption-key test supplies constructed token JSON payloads to encrypt/decrypt/hash preservation across rotation in created schema. The token properties are application test data, not bearer tokens or SQL credentials; actual database connection is explicit operator input.
smoke-runner replaces every child global fetch before importing actual smoke CLI; returned token is fabricated Response consumed by CLI authorization-header flow. No socket is opened for this token.

Qualification Provider reconciler receives encryptedApiKey opaque-fixed metadata for a task-created provider row and tests preservation. SQL auth is explicit MAX490 config, not this marker. No provider completion/real model key issued from opaque marker.

Synthetic HMAC key configures controller spawned/built by test; requests sign with the same local key. Nonce integration owns MySQL/controller lifecycle; workspace test injects nonce store/child-process behavior. Not deployed/shared controller signing material.

Archived curl snippets now contain redacted placeholders. Consumer would be a human executing a development login command; no CI/runtime import executes these Markdown files. They cannot authenticate without replacing placeholder; old revision exposure is retained in history scope.

Archived review quotes an old Gateway hardcoded password as a vulnerability example. Current DirectAdapter does not consume that old Gateway AUTH path. Historical literal remains exposed and must not be treated as evidence of revocation; no current authentication consumer found in this branch.

Archived review illustrates password-to-key update mismatch using JSON payload examples. It is prose, not evaluated source/config; actual current server credential consumers use runtime encrypted input. Historical account validity is not inferred from this example.

collectCancelEvents sends a fixture bearer marker through supplied connect() function. Direct main creates a local DirectAdapter with actorContextService ignoring token and controlled provider; unit tests supply fake sockets. Database side effects in direct mode still require explicit qualification resource authorization.

agent-runtime-mysql creates random schema, local DirectAdapter on port zero and injected authority accepting fixture actor. Synthetic WS token is sent only to that adapter. SQL authentication uses DB_PASSWORD from caller (wrapper now requires presence); no shared JWT signing value used for this marker.

Bootstrap atomicity harness creates disposable MySQL with random loopback port, builds qualification schema and supplies the fixed synthetic admin input to bootstrap in that container. It verifies bcrypt/transaction state there. Standalone fixture is not an existing platform administrator password.

assert-agent-run-failure starts local adapter with injected authenticateAccessToken and FailingProvider; fixture token reaches that listener. It connects to configured DB and inserts synthetic non-login actor; DB target/schema ownership is caller prerequisite, not guaranteed merely by token stub.

Report field historicalT04Tokens is an availability marker for missing historical usage accounting. Consumer is JSON evidence report serialization, not token authentication or provider usage injection.

Startup readiness test owns disposable MySQL random port and spawned API with local fake provider. It initializes qualification admin using same test password then logs into that API. Worker SQL user is created by test in that container. Keys and passwords are local fixture inputs; no existing platform user/DB is selected.

Operations resource controller reads constructed secret fields from mocked authFetch Response, including delayed prior-target results. Consumer is local controller state/discard logic, not external credential storage.

Global fetch is spied/stubbed to return synthetic access/refresh JSON. API session refresh logic consumes these values and tests generation/target invalidation; no refresh endpoint or JWT signer outside mock is called.

Users view form submits its fixed password only to apiClient.post spy initialized in beforeEach. Tests resolve/reject this spy to exercise role assignment and retries; no user is created in a live API.

Network-device form SNMP secrets are captured by mocked authFetch module; synthetic post response is returned and validation/whitespace rules are asserted. No SNMP/device route or native transport is reached.

Feishu/email settings fields are supplied to mocked authFetch POST/PUT and compared against captured request bodies. Transport is replaced at frontend module boundary; channel fixture does not trigger delivery.

LLM config draft/saved key fields feed mocked apiClient post/get/put; model discovery/connection-test calls resolve locally and draft persistence assertions inspect spies. No external Provider is contacted even though URL resembles a vendor.
Resource/instance form credentials go to mocked authFetch implementation returning test-connection/create responses. Assertions compare submitted body/state; no real database connection attempt.
LoginGate test state password is passed to apiClient.directLogin spy and global fetch stub. Trimming/preservation is asserted locally; no login request reaches a service.

A local variable named token is a constructed long example URL, placed in chat history text/code to test wrapping. page.route intercepts API requests before the chat-history fixture renders. No bearer/session token or login verification is involved.

MAX178 spec persists synthetic Provider through real request API, with baseURL set to its created loopback HTTP receiver. run-MAX-178 owns disposable SQL and dedicated Playwright services; direct env flag/DB_PORT/baseURL override do not prove ownership. Key is a fake accepted only by local receiver; API/SQL target authorization remains caller duty.

release-critical paths creates an enabled webhook channel with synthetic signing secret via page.request, then exercises report delivery at the configured Playwright service. It is a real credential consumer and may dispatch notification traffic; public example URL is not proof of a controlled receiver. BaseURL can target an existing service. Target/API/notification receiver authorization must be provided before real execution; no test-directory safety claim.

release-security posts a deliberately incorrect administrator password to the real login endpoint and expects 401. It is a negative authentication attempt, not an issued account. baseURL/managed qualification credentials and caller target ownership remain required.

Revocation spec creates a unique qualification username with a matching synthetic password, logs in as that account, revokes and finally cleans up. This is real authentication/write at Playwright request.baseURL; admin password is now injected. Managed bootstrap provides qualification admin but direct/override target requires explicit caller ownership; fixed per-test user input must never be used to justify shared account reuse.

Security spec submits private-URL negative input and creates disabled synthetic notification channel then cleans up. Playwright baseURL is real, can be overridden; accepted channel is disabled and no send is requested here, but caller still must own selected platform and its collector context.

Security spec creates synthetic instance metadata for unsupported MongoDB target and validates capability behavior; password is stored via real API at Playwright baseURL. Unsupported collection path is expected to reject; target/API ownership must be supplied by managed qualification setup or caller.

resource-diagnosis installs page.route for auth/refresh returning synthetic token pair before authFetch request; rotation-probe route is also fulfilled locally. No real refresh account is contacted through those matched responses.

max238-unbind-preview owns labeled random-name MySQL container with loopback published port and empty fixture password; passes that port/password to collect-now operation-recovery test. Handle/label checks constrain cleanup. Empty value belongs to this created fixture, not a fallback for an unspecified resource.

Investigation fixture bcrypt-hashes ownerPassword into its newly created t06_workspace random schema, starts local API/WS/Vite and returns this fixture context. DB root login is a separate T06_TEST_MYSQL_PASSWORD; browser owner password is task-local. Caller still must supply authorized SQL server/port.

Instance host diagnostic spec uses page.request to create synthetic database instance metadata with task username, then controls host evidence/analysis routes and cleans created IDs. Playwright baseURL can be existing/overridden; no proof that arbitrary API or later background collection is isolated. Requires managed qualification target/caller resource authorization.
